extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, advocates, and other comment drafters submitting administrative-rule comments who want to preserve issues for judicial review under the State Farm hard-look doctrine
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting notice-and-comment submissions that preserve objections for arbitrary-and-capricious (State Farm) judicial review by putting specific factors, alternatives, factual challenges, and legal authorities on the rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Farm hard-look doctrine (agency duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under State Farm, an agency must (1) articulate the policies it purports to further; (2) show that the chosen course is reasonable in light of relevant policies, alternatives, and facts; (3) demonstrate that findings have support in the rulemaking record; and (4) show consideration of important aspects of the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these four duties as the legal standard to frame objections. A comment can point to failures in any of these four duties to argue arbitrary-and-capricious review. (Source: Motor Vehicle Mfrs. Ass'n v. State Farm Mut. Auto. Ins. Co., 463 U.S. 29 (1983).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Add a specific factor to the rulemaking record
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment add a specific factor (data, fact, perspective) to the rulemaking record?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective comments put a specific factor on the record — e.g., a downstream effect, a cost the agency overlooked, or a population at risk — that the agency must address or risk reversal. Be concrete about the factor so the agency cannot say the issue was not raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name a specific viable alternative and explain reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment name a specific viable alternative and explain why it is reasonable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hard-look review requires consideration of reasonable alternatives. A good comment names a specific viable alternative, and ideally supplies implementing detail (how it would be implemented, cost estimates, regulatory text, or procedural steps) to show the alternative is realistic and reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge specific factual findings or data the agency relies on
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment challenge specific factual findings or data the agency relies on?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because agency findings must have record support, a strong comment identifies particular findings that lack record support or are contradicted by evidence. Cite record materials or external data that directly refute or undermine the agency's factual basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect each objection to a specific statutory or E.O. authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment connect each objection to a specific statutory or EO authority?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hard-look review tests reasonableness in light of the agency's statutory authority. Explain why the agency's chosen course departs from statutory text, statutory purpose, or applicable executive orders; link objections to the governing legal standard rather than only to policy preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precise language that could be quoted in litigation papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment use precise language that could be quoted in litigation papers?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft objections in clear, specific, and quotable language so they can be incorporated into a judicial brief. Avoid vague or conclusory phrasing; state the objection, the supporting facts or law, and the requested action succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify 'important aspects of the problem' the agency overlooked
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment identify 'important aspects of the problem' the agency overlooked?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out material aspects the agency failed to consider (e.g., disparate impacts, indirect effects, compliance burdens). Showing omission of important aspects supports a claim that the agency failed to consider relevant factors under State Farm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise issues with sufficient specificity to preserve them for judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment raise each issue with sufficient specificity so it will not be deemed waived for judicial purposes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vague or generalized complaints are often treated as waived. Make each objection specific (what, why, and under what legal standard), tie it to the record, and explain the relief or alternative sought to maximize the chance courts will review the issue.
